questions.question: What does calling a generator function such as `countdown(3)` do immediately?
options: Runs the whole body and returns a list
Runs the body up to the first yield
Returns a generator object without executing any of the body
questions.explanation: Calling a generator function only creates a generator object. The body starts running on the first next() call and pauses at each yield.

questions.question: Given `squares = (n * n for n in range(4))`, what does calling `sum(squares)` twice return?
questions.explanation: Generators are single-use. The first sum consumes every value; the exhausted generator yields nothing afterwards, so the second sum is 0 with no error.

questions.question: Which pair of methods defines the iterator protocol for an iterator object?
options: __iter__ returning the iterator itself, and __next__ returning the next value or raising StopIteration
questions.explanation: An iterator implements __next__ (raising StopIteration when done) and an __iter__ that returns itself. An iterable only needs __iter__ returning a fresh iterator.

questions.question: In a recursive `flatten` generator, what does `yield from flatten(item)` do?
options: Returns the entire flattened sub-list as a single value
Starts a new thread for the sub-generator
Yields only the first item of the sub-generator
Yields every item produced by the sub-generator, also forwarding send() and throw() and evaluating to its return value
questions.explanation: yield from delegates to the sub-iterable, yielding each of its items in turn; with sub-generators it also forwards send()/throw() and evaluates to the sub-generator's return value.
